question: What is the main role of a midwife when it comes to nutrition during antenatal care?

options.A: Prescribing high-dose medications for severe malnutrition
options.B: Translating dietary concepts into practical advice for mothers
options.C: Conducting laboratory blood sugar tests for pregnant women
options.D: Formulating synthetic vitamin supplements for clinics

explanation: Midwives help mothers understand how to use local foods for a healthy pregnancy. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is knowing about nutrition so important in midwifery practice?

options.A: Midwives are legally required to manage severe clinical malnutrition alone
options.B: Fetal development is entirely unaffected by the maternal diet
options.C: Pregnancy and lactation drastically increase a woman's physiological demands
options.D: Standard hospital diets are always completely sufficient for pregnant women

explanation: The growing baby and milk production require extra nutrients, making proper maternal nutrition vital. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is one main function of food for the body?

options.A: Providing fuel for physical activity and metabolism
options.B: Preventing all genetic mutations in the fetus
options.C: Eliminating the need for any water consumption
options.D: Directly replacing the function of human hormones

explanation: Food serves as the body's main energy source to power daily activities and basic metabolic functions. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h2)

question: A pregnant woman asks why she needs to eat both beans and maize instead of just one. What is the best reason?

options.A: Only animal-based foods can ever provide energy to the body
options.B: Plant foods have no actual nutritional value during pregnancy
options.C: Combining different food sources ensures a complete supply of tissue-building materials
options.D: Eating only one type of food will immediately cause complete organ failure

explanation: Different foods supply varied nutrients needed for growth, repair, and overall body regulation. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h2)

question: What does the process of nutrition involve inside the body?

options.A: The direct conversion of food into red blood cells
options.B: Only the physical act of chewing and swallowing meals
options.C: Ingestion, digestion, absorption, and cellular utilization of nutrients
options.D: Exclusively the elimination of waste products through the kidneys

explanation: Nutrition covers the full journey of food from intake to how individual cells use those chemical components. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h3)

question: How does good nutrition help protect a pregnant woman against infections?

options.A: It stops all microorganisms from entering the household
options.B: It creates a physical barrier on the skin against bacteria
options.C: It acts as a direct antibiotic drug killing malaria parasites
options.D: It strengthens her immune function and overall physiological defenses

explanation: A well-nourished body maintains a strong immune system capable of fighting off common illnesses. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which category includes nutrients required by the body in large daily amounts?

options.A: Micronutrients
options.B: Macronutrients
options.C: Synthetic enzymes
options.D: Trace elements

explanation: Macronutrients like carbohydrates, proteins, and fats are needed in large quantities to sustain the body. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why can a shortage of a micronutrient still cause health problems even though it is needed in small amounts?

options.A: They make up the bulk of muscle tissue and physical body weight
options.B: They are the only substances that provide calories for energy
options.C: They act as vital helpers for essential chemical and enzymatic reactions
options.D: The body cannot store any micronutrient for more than one hour

explanation: Even in tiny amounts, micronutrients regulate critical bodily processes without which serious health issues occur. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h4)

question: What term describes eating enough calories while lacking essential vitamins and minerals?

options.A: Caloric surplus
options.B: Hidden hunger
options.C: Basal starvation
options.D: Macronutrient overload

explanation: Hidden hunger refers to micronutrient deficiencies that happen even when a person eats enough food to feel full. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which meal plan is a good example of a balanced local diet for an antenatal client in Nigeria?

options.A: A large bowl of white rice eaten completely plain with water
options.B: Fried dough snacks paired with a bottled sugary carbonated drink
options.C: Only roasted maize consumed throughout the entire morning
options.D: Eba with egusi soup, fish, and a side of steamed spinach

explanation: This meal combines carbohydrates, protein, fats, and protective vitamins from vegetables into a balanced dish. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which tool do midwives commonly use to quickly check nutritional status in community settings?

options.A: Routine invasive liver biopsy needles
options.B: Intravenous glucose tolerance monitors
options.C: Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) tape
options.D: Advanced magnetic resonance imaging

explanation: MUAC tapes are portable, quick, and effective for screening undernutrition during antenatal outreach. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is NOT a typical complication linked to maternal overnutrition during pregnancy?

options.A: Obstructed labor from a large baby
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Severe irreversible bone marrow failure
options.D: Pregnancy-induced hypertension

explanation: Overnutrition leads to metabolic and mechanical pregnancy complications like diabetes and high blood pressure, not bone marrow failure. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main role of food in the body beyond satisfying hunger?

options.A: Increasing physical height during adulthood
options.B: Replacing the need for clean drinking water
options.C: Preventing all known genetic disorders
options.D: Providing biochemical materials for life and energy

explanation: Food serves as the fundamental source of raw materials and energy needed to sustain all cellular and metabolic processes in the body. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is basic nutritional knowledge important for a midwife?

options.A: It replaces the need to prescribe routine iron supplements
options.B: It guarantees that babies will be born without any birth defects
options.C: It allows midwives to diagnose complex gastrointestinal diseases
options.D: It helps connect traditional diets with evidence-based maternal needs

explanation: Midwives use nutritional science to guide mothers wisely, respecting local food practices while ensuring clinical dietary requirements are met. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which nutrient class serves as the body's fastest and preferred source of energy?

options.A: Water
options.B: Vitamins
options.C: Carbohydrates
options.D: Minerals

explanation: Carbohydrates break down quickly into glucose, making them the primary and fastest fuel source for cellular activity. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h2)

question: An expecting mother asks why she feels tired even when resting. What concept explains the energy her body uses just to stay alive at rest?

options.A: Enzymatic hydrolysis
options.B: Gastrointestinal transit
options.C: Nutritional assimilation
options.D: Basal metabolic rate

explanation: The basal metabolic rate represents the baseline energy expenditure required by the body to maintain vital physiological functions while at rest. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h2)

question: What are the individual chemical building blocks that join together to form proteins?

options.A: Monosaccharides
options.B: Fatty acids
options.C: Amino acids
options.D: Nucleotides

explanation: Proteins are long chains composed of smaller units known as amino acids, which are essential for tissue growth and repair. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why does a pregnant woman have a much higher need for tissue-building nutrients?

options.A: To prevent the sudden accumulation of excessive body fat
options.B: To support the growth of the fetus, placenta, and expanded blood volume
options.C: To lower her basal metabolic rate during the third trimester
options.D: To completely stop the normal process of cellular turnover

explanation: Pregnancy involves massive anatomical changes and tissue creation, requiring a steady supply of structural building blocks. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which nutrient is specifically critical during early pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Folic acid
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Folic acid plays a vital role in DNA synthesis and the proper closure of the neural tube during the earliest weeks of embryonic development. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h4)

question: How do vitamins and minerals generally function within human metabolism?

options.A: As heavy storage molecules for long-term lipid reserves
options.B: As the exclusive structural framework for skeletal bone development
options.C: As regulatory agents and coenzymes that support vital chemical reactions
options.D: As the primary source of calories for basal metabolic activities

explanation: Micronutrients regulate metabolic pathways, support immune function, and act as coenzymes rather than serving as major fuel sources. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h4)

question: A pregnant patient shows signs of anemia due to the expansion of her blood volume. Which dietary nutrient must be emphasized in her care?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Iron
options.D: Carbohydrate

explanation: Blood volume expansion during pregnancy creates a high demand for iron to synthesize adequate hemoglobin and prevent maternal anemia. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main danger of the traditional belief that pregnant women should restrict their food intake?

options.A: It causes an immediate drop in basal metabolic rate to zero
options.B: It completely stops the production of amniotic fluid
options.C: It increases the risk of low birth weight and maternal depletion
options.D: It permanently prevents the natural expansion of blood volume

explanation: Restricting food intake denies the mother and fetus essential nutrients, leading to poor fetal growth and depleting maternal nutrient stores. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T2#BMP118_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary role of accessory organs like the pancreas and liver in digestion?

options.A: Producing and secreting digestive enzymes and fluids
options.B: Absorbing water and solidifying waste materials
options.C: Swallowing food from the oral cavity into the pharynx
options.D: Storing excess dietary fat within mucosal cells

explanation: Accessory organs release vital juices and enzymes into the digestive tract to break down food chemically. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary task of the gastrointestinal tract?

options.A: Breaking down food mechanically
options.B: Eliminating undigested waste
options.C: Absorbing nutrients into the blood
options.D: Synthesizing new red blood cells

explanation: The gastrointestinal tract handles digestion, absorption, and waste removal, while red blood cells are made in the bone marrow. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h1)

question: What primary digestive function does saliva perform in the oral cavity?

options.A: It neutralizes all stomach acid before food arrives.
options.B: It completely digests proteins into free amino acids.
options.C: It starts the breakdown of carbohydrates using amylase.
options.D: It absorbs simple sugars directly through the tongue.

explanation: Saliva contains the enzyme salivary amylase, which begins breaking down starches into simpler sugars right inside the mouth. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why does the body close the epiglottis during the act of swallowing?

options.A: To prevent food and liquid from entering the airway
options.B: To trigger extra saliva production in the throat
options.C: To push air upward into the nasal passages
options.D: To slow down the movement of the food bolus

explanation: The epiglottis acts as a lid over the trachea during swallowing to ensure food goes safely into the esophagus instead of the lungs. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which specific cells in the stomach lining secrete hydrochloric acid?

options.A: Parietal cells
options.B: Chief cells
options.C: Mucous cells
options.D: Goblet cells

explanation: Parietal cells are responsible for producing hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor in the stomach. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is the production of intrinsic factor by the stomach clinically significant?

options.A: It is required for absorbing vitamin B12 further down the gut.
options.B: It directly digests dietary protein into absorbable peptides.
options.C: It stimulates the pancreas to release digestive enzymes.
options.D: It coats the stomach wall to prevent ulcer formation.

explanation: Intrinsic factor binds to vitamin B12 so it can be successfully absorbed in the lower small intestine, preventing pernicious anemia. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary function of bile salts in fat digestion?

options.A: Emulsifying large fat droplets into smaller droplets
options.B: Directly breaking triglycerides down into amino acids
options.C: Absorbing water-soluble vitamins into the bloodstream
options.D: Neutralizing stomach acid in the large intestine

explanation: Bile breaks large fat masses into tiny droplets, increasing the surface area for enzymes to digest fats effectively. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which organ secretes the bicarbonate needed to neutralize acidic chyme entering the small intestine?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Gallbladder
options.C: Salivary gland
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: The pancreas releases alkaline fluid containing bicarbonate to neutralize the harsh acid coming from the stomach. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do digested fats enter lacteals instead of standard blood capillaries directly?

options.A: Blood capillaries completely reject all forms of dietary lipids.
options.B: They are converted into simple sugars before entering the blood.
options.C: They require high levels of stomach acid to enter the bloodstream.
options.D: They are packaged into chylomicrons which are too large for capillaries.

explanation: Lipids reassemble into large chylomicrons inside intestinal cells, forcing them to enter the more permeable lymphatic lacteals first. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h5)

question: What structural feature of the small intestine primarily increases its surface area for absorption?

options.A: Hepatic portal veins
options.B: Muscular sphincter rings
options.C: Villi and microvilli
options.D: Gastric rugae folds

explanation: Tiny finger-like projections called villi and microvilli create a huge surface area to maximize nutrient uptake. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine regarding digestive contents?

options.A: Absorbing water and electrolytes to form solid feces
options.B: Emulsifying dietary fats into smaller lipid droplets
options.C: Secreting the majority of digestive enzymes for proteins
options.D: Initiating the mechanical process of mastication

explanation: The colon removes water and salts from unabsorbed waste residue, turning liquid material into formed stool. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h6)

question: What helpful role do resident bacteria play in the human colon?

options.A: Fermenting fiber and producing certain vitamins
options.B: Secreting bile acids to digest remaining dietary fats
options.C: Producing intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 uptake
options.D: Breaking down complex proteins into amino acids

explanation: Gut microbes break down fibers we cannot digest and synthesize valuable nutrients like vitamin K for the host. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a frequent consequence of chronic malabsorption in pregnant women?

options.A: Rapid overgrowth of beneficial gut bacteria
options.B: Excessive accumulation of liver bile pigments
options.C: Nutritional deficiencies like maternal anemia
options.D: Hyperactive salivary enzyme production

explanation: When the gut cannot absorb vital micronutrients like iron and folate, the pregnant woman easily develops nutritional anemia. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which clinical presentation in an infant should alert a midwife to possible digestive malabsorption?

options.A: Rapid closure of the cranial fontanelles
options.B: Strong preference for breast milk over water
options.C: Poor weight gain and chronic diarrhea
options.D: High frequency of spontaneous smiling

explanation: Inability to absorb nutrients manifests clearly as failure to gain weight properly, often accompanied by abnormal stool patterns. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary chemical form of energy used by cells in the human body?

options.A: Fatty acid chains
options.B: Glycogen molecules
options.C: Amino acid polymers
options.D: Adenosine triphosphate

explanation: ATP is the main energy currency that cells use to power various metabolic processes and maintain vital functions. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which component of total energy expenditure typically accounts for the largest variation between two different people?

options.A: Voluntary physical activity
options.B: Thermic effect of food
options.C: Fetal growth demands
options.D: Basal metabolic processes

explanation: While resting processes take up most daily energy, physical activity levels differ greatly from person to person, causing the biggest variation in overall energy use. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h1)

question: What percentage of total daily energy expenditure does BMR typically account for in a sedentary adult?

options.A: Sixty to seventy-five percent
options.B: Zero to ten percent
options.C: Twenty to thirty percent
options.D: Eighty to ninety percent

explanation: BMR makes up the largest portion of daily energy use because the body's internal organs constantly require fuel just to stay alive. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why do clinicians frequently measure Resting Energy Expenditure instead of true Basal Metabolic Rate?

options.A: True BMR can only be calculated during active physical exercise.
options.B: BMR only measures energy used by the skeletal muscles.
options.C: REE does not require the strict fasting and laboratory conditions of BMR.
options.D: REE provides a much lower and safer estimate for pregnant women.

explanation: Measuring true BMR requires strict fasting and complete rest that is hard to manage in routine clinics, so REE is used as a practical alternative. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which type of body tissue is the most metabolically active and burns the most calories at rest?

options.A: Lean muscle tissue
options.B: Subcutaneous fat tissue
options.C: Visceral adipose tissue
options.D: Connective joint tissue

explanation: Lean tissue requires much more energy to maintain itself than fat tissue, meaning more muscle leads to a higher resting metabolism. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h3)

question: How do thyroid hormones directly affect a person's basal metabolic rate?

options.A: They slow down heart rate to conserve energy during sleep.
options.B: They regulate the speed at which cells consume oxygen and produce energy.
options.C: They decrease the thermic effect of food in the digestive tract.
options.D: They stimulate the storage of excess glucose into subcutaneous fat.

explanation: Thyroid hormones act as the body's metabolic thermostat, controlling how quickly cells use energy and generate heat. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h3)

question: What happens to the basal metabolic rate during a fever?

options.A: It increases by about 10 to 13 percent for every degree Celsius rise.
options.B: It remains completely unchanged until the fever breaks naturally.
options.C: It drops significantly to help the body fight off the infection.
options.D: It shifts entirely to burning stored carbohydrates instead of fat.

explanation: Elevated body temperature speeds up chemical reactions in the body, causing a noticeable increase in resting energy needs. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why does the body naturally lower its BMR during periods of prolonged starvation?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of remaining food in the gut
options.B: To prepare the thyroid gland for producing extra hormones
options.C: To conserve energy and protect vital life-sustaining functions
options.D: To increase the rate at which proteins are built in muscles

explanation: Starvation triggers a survival mechanism where the body slows down its metabolic engine to make limited energy reserves last longer. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h4)

question: What generally happens to a woman's basal metabolic rate by the third trimester of pregnancy?

options.A: It decreases by about 10 percent
options.B: It drops to zero to protect the fetus
options.C: It stays exactly the same as pre-pregnancy
options.D: It increases by 15 to 25 percent

explanation: The metabolic demands of supporting a growing fetus and maternal tissues cause a substantial rise in BMR by late pregnancy. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h5)

question: A pregnant woman in her third trimester reports constant fatigue and poor weight gain despite eating her usual pre-pregnancy portions. What is the most likely physiological explanation?

options.A: Her increased BMR and fetal demands require more calories than her current intake.
options.B: Her digestive tract has slowed down to absorb less food.
options.C: Her thyroid gland has completely stopped producing hormones.
options.D: Her body has lowered its metabolic rate to store more fat.

explanation: Late pregnancy raises energy requirements significantly, so eating normal pre-pregnancy amounts will lead to a deficit, causing fatigue and poor weight gain. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary nutrient category that serves as the main source of energy for a pregnant woman?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Fats
options.C: Vitamins
options.D: Proteins

explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, which is the body's main and fastest source of energy for both the mother and the growing baby. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body naturally develop insulin resistance as pregnancy progresses?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of dietary proteins
options.B: To keep more glucose circulating in the blood for the growing fetus
options.C: To prevent the pancreas from producing too much insulin
options.D: To help the mother store more fat in her lower limbs

explanation: Natural insulin resistance makes maternal cells take up less glucose, leaving more available in the bloodstream to cross the placenta to the baby. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is classified as a monosaccharide?

options.A: Lactose
options.B: Sucrose
options.C: Starch
options.D: Glucose

explanation: Glucose is a single-unit sugar, making it a monosaccharide, whereas sucrose and lactose have two units and starch has many. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h2)

question: How do complex carbohydrates differ from simple sugars in their effect on the body?

options.A: Simple sugars contain high amounts of protective dietary fiber.
options.B: Simple sugars are stored in the liver as long-chain starches.
options.C: Complex carbohydrates digest slowly and provide steady energy over a longer period.
options.D: Complex carbohydrates enter the bloodstream instantly without needing any digestion.

explanation: The long chains of starch and fiber take time to break down, preventing the rapid sugar spikes caused by simple sugars. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of a whole grain rich in complex carbohydrates?

options.A: Ofada rice
options.B: White sugar
options.C: Table syrup
options.D: Processed wheat flour

explanation: Ofada rice is an unrefined local grain that retains its outer bran layer, offering valuable fiber and complex carbohydrates. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h3)

question: A pregnant woman complains of sluggishness and asks which local food will give her sustained energy without sudden sugar crashes. What is the best recommendation?

options.A: White bread with sugary jam
options.B: Sponge cake made with refined white flour
options.C: Boiled sweet potatoes or yam with vegetables
options.D: Sweetened bottled fruit juice

explanation: Whole tubers and vegetables provide complex carbohydrates and fiber that release energy slowly into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which specific organ in the developing fetus relies almost entirely on glucose for its proper function?

options.A: Skin
options.B: Kidneys
options.C: Brain
options.D: Bones

explanation: The fetal brain has a high metabolic demand and depends heavily on a continuous supply of glucose from the maternal circulation. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is dietary fiber especially important for preventing constipation during pregnancy?

options.A: It speeds up the absorption of water in the stomach.
options.B: It adds bulk to the stool and encourages regular bowel movements.
options.C: It turns into pure glucose to fuel intestinal muscles.
options.D: It directly stops the production of pregnancy hormones.

explanation: Fiber does not digest in the gut, so it remains in the bowel where it absorbs water and creates bulk to stimulate muscle contractions. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the term for high blood sugar that is first recognized during pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.B: Placental abruption
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Maternal hypoglycemia

explanation: Gestational diabetes mellitus develops when pregnant women cannot produce enough insulin to handle the body's natural insulin resistance. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h5)

question: What happens to the body when a pregnant woman eats very few carbohydrates over a long period of time?

options.A: The mother's blood pressure drops to dangerous levels.
options.B: The placenta stops producing progesterone immediately.
options.C: The body breaks down fats for energy, producing harmful ketones.
options.D: The baby grows much faster than normal inside the womb.

explanation: Without enough dietary carbohydrate for fuel, fat breakdown creates ketones, which can cross the placenta and pose risks to fetal development. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the main job of iodine in the human body?

options.A: Forming thyroid hormones
options.B: Building strong bone matrices
options.C: Transporting oxygen in blood
options.D: Regulating fluid balance

explanation: Iodine is a trace element that the body needs specifically to make thyroxine and triiodothyronine. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why are trace elements like iodine a big concern in certain geographic areas?

options.A: Human bodies store trace minerals for only one day
options.B: Local soils often lack sufficient iodine content
options.C: Cooking methods completely destroy all mineral traces
options.D: Trace minerals are only found in processed foods

explanation: Crops and farm animals raised on soil low in iodine cannot provide enough of this mineral through the natural food chain. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h1)

question: At what point in pregnancy does the baby's thyroid gland start working on its own?

options.A: At birth only
options.B: In the third trimester
options.C: Around twelve weeks
options.D: By four weeks

explanation: Before the fetal thyroid begins working around twelve weeks, the developing baby depends entirely on maternal hormones. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h2)

question: Why do pregnant women need more dietary iodine than non-pregnant women?

options.A: Her bones require extra iodine to expand during labor
options.B: Her body stops absorbing iron and must rely solely on iodine
options.C: Her stomach acid destroys most trace minerals during gestation
options.D: Her kidneys clear iodide faster and she supports fetal brain development

explanation: Faster kidney filtration along with the high metabolic needs of the growing baby increase the daily iodine requirement. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is the main public health method used to prevent iodine deficiency in areas far from the coast?

options.A: Fortified flour
options.B: Vitamin C supplements
options.C: Iodized drinking water
options.D: Iodized salt

explanation: Adding iodine to table salt is the most effective and widespread public health strategy for delivering iodine to inland populations. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which food group naturally contains the highest amount of iodine?

options.A: Root vegetables
options.B: Refined cereal grains
options.C: Citrus fruits
options.D: Seafood and marine fish

explanation: Oceans are naturally rich in iodine, making marine life and seaweeds abundant sources of the mineral. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h3)

question: In what chemical form does the body absorb dietary iodine from the gut?

options.A: Thyroglobulin
options.B: Iodide
options.C: Potassium iodate
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Food compounds are broken down into iodide ions before crossing the intestinal wall into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h4)

question: How does the body get rid of extra iodine that the thyroid gland does not use?

options.A: By storage in long-term bone matrices
options.B: Through breakdown by liver enzymes
options.C: Through renal excretion in the urine
options.D: Via exhalation through the lungs

explanation: The kidneys filter out unneeded iodine, which is why urine tests are used to check iodine levels in a population. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h4)

question: What physical sign usually appears when the thyroid gland swells due to a lack of iodine?

options.A: Jaundice
options.B: Petechiae
options.C: Goiter
options.D: Edema

explanation: Constant stimulation causes the thyroid gland to swell, creating a visible lump on the front of the neck called a goiter. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h5)

question: What is the most serious effect of severe iodine deficiency during pregnancy on the baby?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Neural tube defects
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Cretinism

explanation: A severe lack of thyroid hormones during early brain development leads to permanent physical and mental impairment known as cretinism. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h5)

question: What practical tip should a midwife give a pregnant woman about using iodized salt at home?

options.A: Add salt near the end of cooking and store it in a covered container
options.B: Boil the salt in water for ten minutes before adding it to food
options.C: Keep the salt package open on the counter so it stays dry
options.D: Rinse the salt under running water to remove bitter chemical tastes

explanation: Heat and exposure to air can cause iodine to evaporate, so proper storage and adding it late in cooking preserve the nutrient. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a midwife's routine iodine check during an antenatal booking visit?

options.A: Asking if the family uses iodized table salt at home
options.B: Testing deep tendon reflexes with a neurological hammer
options.C: Palpating the front of the neck for signs of thyroid swelling
options.D: Asking about regular household consumption of seafood

explanation: Reflex testing is part of a general physical exam rather than a specific nutritional assessment for iodine status like neck palpation. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T10#BMP118_U2_T10_h6)

question: What type of nutrient is zinc classified as based on the amount the body requires?

options.A: A macronutrient for energy
options.B: An electrolyte solution
options.C: A trace element or micromineral
options.D: A water-soluble vitamin

explanation: Zinc is required in small quantities by the body, which places it in the category of trace elements or microminerals rather than macronutrients. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is it important to get zinc in your diet every single day?

options.A: Zinc is rapidly destroyed by stomach acid every day
options.B: The kidneys filter out all stored zinc within hours
options.C: The body lacks a dedicated storage depot for zinc
options.D: Micro minerals cannot bind to proteins for storage

explanation: Because the human body does not maintain a specialized storage organ for zinc, it depends on a continuous daily supply from food. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h1)

question: How many enzymes in the human body rely on zinc for catalytic, structural, or regulatory functions?

options.A: Over three hundred enzymes
options.B: Exactly ten enzymes
options.C: Fewer than twenty enzymes
options.D: Roughly fifty enzymes

explanation: Zinc is a crucial component for the proper functioning of more than three hundred different enzymes involved in various metabolic pathways. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h2)

question: Why does the body need more zinc during pregnancy?

options.A: The mother needs extra zinc to produce breast milk immediately
options.B: Hormonal changes destroy the body's natural zinc reserves
options.C: Red blood cell volume decreases and forces zinc out
options.D: Rapid fetal cell division and placental transport require it

explanation: The rapid growth of fetal tissues and the work of the placenta create a high demand for zinc during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which food group provides the highest amount of easily absorbed zinc?

options.A: Leafy green vegetables and tubers
options.B: Sweet fruits and citrus juices
options.C: Animal proteins like red meat and fish
options.D: Refined white flour and polished rice

explanation: Animal-source foods contain zinc in forms that are readily used by the human body without plant compounds blocking absorption. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h3)

question: A pregnant woman in a local Nigerian community asks which common local staples can help improve her zinc intake. Which group should you recommend?

options.A: Refined starch and sugary beverages
options.B: Imported white bread and soft drinks
options.C: Cassava flakes and sweet potato slices
options.D: Cowpeas, melon seeds, and whole grains

explanation: Local legumes like cowpeas, oil seeds like egusi or melon seeds, and whole cereal grains are practical local sources of zinc. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h3)

question: In which part of the digestive tract is most zinc absorbed?

options.A: Gallbladder and bile ducts
options.B: Duodenum and upper jejunum
options.C: Stomach and lower esophagus
options.D: Large colon and rectum

explanation: The early sections of the small intestine, specifically the duodenum and upper jejunum, serve as the primary sites for zinc uptake into the body. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h4)

question: Which substance found in unrefined plant foods binds to zinc and reduces its absorption?

options.A: Phytates
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Lactose

explanation: Phytates bind to minerals like zinc in the gut, making them difficult for the body to absorb. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why can measuring blood zinc levels during pregnancy sometimes be misleading?

options.A: Expanding maternal blood volume dilutes the concentration in the blood
options.B: The placenta destroys half of the circulating zinc in the plasma
options.C: Routine iron supplements block accurate laboratory testing
options.D: Fetal hormones artificially spike the levels of free zinc

explanation: The natural expansion of blood volume during pregnancy dilutes the blood, which can lower mineral test results even if tissue stores are adequate. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h5)

question: Which phase of motherhood places a continuous daily demand on maternal zinc stores through milk production?

options.A: Menstruation
options.B: Lactation
options.C: Ovulation
options.D: Implantation

explanation: Breastfeeding requires a steady transfer of nutrients from the mother to the baby, drawing heavily on maternal zinc reserves during the postpartum period. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h5)

question: Which body system usually shows signs of trouble first when a person lacks enough zinc?

options.A: Respiratory system
options.B: Skeletal system
options.C: Immune system
options.D: Cardiovascular system

explanation: Immune function relies heavily on zinc for white blood cell activity, making frequent infections an early sign of deficiency. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized complication of severe zinc deficiency in pregnancy?

options.A: Permanent maternal vision loss
options.B: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.C: Prolonged or difficult labor
options.D: Premature rupture of membranes

explanation: While severe zinc deficiency causes growth restriction, prolonged labor, and membrane complications, permanent blindness is primarily associated with vitamin A deficiency, not zinc. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h6)

question: Taking very high doses of zinc supplements can block the absorption of which other mineral?

options.A: Iodine
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Copper
options.D: Sodium

explanation: High levels of zinc in the gut trigger proteins that trap copper in intestinal cells, preventing its absorption and leading to deficiency. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h7)

question: What is the main danger of taking very high doses of zinc supplements for a long time?

options.A: Rapid bone calcification and sudden joint stiffness
options.B: Suppressed immune function and copper deficiency anemia
options.C: Uncontrollable weight gain due to metabolic slowing
options.D: Severe dehydration from chronic excessive urination

explanation: Excessive zinc intake disrupts copper metabolism, resulting in anemia and weakening the immune system. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h7)

question: During an antenatal health talk, a midwife wants to help mothers maximize the zinc they get from local plant foods. What preparation method should she emphasize?

options.A: Frying all plant foods in high heat to destroy anti-nutrients instantly
options.B: Soaking, fermenting, or germinating grains and legumes before cooking
options.C: Rinsing cooked beans repeatedly in cold water right before serving
options.D: Blending raw grains into cold water and drinking them immediately

explanation: Traditional preparation steps like soaking, sprouting, and fermentation activate enzymes that break down phytates, making plant zinc easier to absorb. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h8)

question: Why should nutrition counseling during antenatal care address local food taboos?

options.A: Taboos often prevent mothers from consuming valuable animal proteins rich in zinc
options.B: Cultural beliefs are the sole scientific cause of gestational diabetes
options.C: Ignoring food taboos prevents the kidneys from filtering trace minerals
options.D: Local customs automatically double the daily requirement for iron

explanation: Many cultural restrictions stop pregnant women from eating nutrient-dense foods like eggs, meat, or fish, which worsens micronutrient deficiencies. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h8)

question: What daily intake defines trace minerals in the human body?

options.A: More than five hundred milligrams
options.B: Between one and two grams
options.C: Exactly ten grams
options.D: Less than 100 milligrams

explanation: Micro minerals are needed in tiny amounts, specifically under 100 milligrams daily, unlike macro minerals which are needed in larger quantities. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why do pregnant women need more of certain micro minerals?

options.A: To compensate for the mother eating less food overall
options.B: To slow down the metabolism of the developing baby
options.C: To support maternal physiological changes and fetal growth
options.D: To replace the weight lost during the first trimester

explanation: Pregnancy creates extra demand on the mother's body to build new tissues, blood, and bones for both her and the baby. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h1)

question: What compound does fluoride form when it joins with tooth enamel?

options.A: Potassium phosphate
options.B: Calcium carbonate
options.C: Fluorapatite
options.D: Sodium chloride

explanation: Fluoride binds with tooth minerals to create fluorapatite, which resists decay much better than regular tooth enamel. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h2)

question: How does fluoride intake during pregnancy help the unborn child?

options.A: It contributes to the mineral matrix of developing tooth buds
options.B: It completely stops the baby from ever getting a cavity
options.C: It whitens the primary teeth before they even erupt
options.D: It softens the gums to make teething completely painless

explanation: Taking in fluoride while pregnant helps build the foundation for the baby's primary teeth forming inside the womb. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h2)

question: Where does the body mostly absorb ingested fluoride?

options.A: Stomach and upper small intestine
options.B: Large intestine and rectum
options.C: Esophagus during swallowing
options.D: Bile duct and gallbladder

explanation: Fluoride is absorbed quickly through the walls of the stomach and the start of the small intestine. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h3)

question: What happens to fluoride that the bones and teeth do not absorb?

options.A: It is stored indefinitely inside the liver tissue
options.B: It is filtered and excreted mainly through the kidneys
options.C: It transforms back into raw elemental fluorine
options.D: It turns into gas and leaves through the lungs

explanation: The body removes extra fluoride through urine via the kidneys. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h3)

question: At about what gestational age do primary tooth buds start to form in a fetus?

options.A: By the end of the second trimester
options.B: Around the sixth week of gestation
options.C: Only during the final month before birth
options.D: Immediately after the baby takes its first breath

explanation: Baby teeth begin developing very early in pregnancy, long before the baby is born. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which bone-building cells are stimulated by fluoride?

options.A: Fibroblasts
options.B: Osteoclasts
options.C: Erythrocytes
options.D: Osteoblasts

explanation: Osteoblasts are the cells that build bone, and fluoride helps stimulate their activity to strengthen bones. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is usually the main source of systemic fluoride for communities?

options.A: Drinking water supplies
options.B: Imported citrus fruits
options.C: Processed dairy products
options.D: Fresh green leafy vegetables

explanation: Public drinking water is commonly the main way people get fluoride in their daily diet. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why should a midwife check local water sources before suggesting fluoride supplements to an expectant mother?

options.A: To avoid accidental overexposure if local water already has high levels
options.B: To calculate the exact monthly cost of buying bottled water instead
options.C: To ensure the water is cold enough for optimal mineral absorption
options.D: To check if the water supply contains harmful bacteria like typhoid

explanation: Checking local water mineral levels prevents too much fluoride intake, which can lead to toxicity. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h5)

question: What condition happens from getting too much fluoride while teeth are forming?

options.A: Goiter
options.B: Scurvy
options.C: Dental fluorosis
options.D: Rickets

explanation: Excess fluoride while teeth form under the gums causes dental fluorosis, which often shows up as white spots on the enamel. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign of severe skeletal fluorosis from long-term high exposure?

options.A: Changes in bone mineral structure
options.B: Sudden and complete hair loss
options.C: Reduced flexibility in the spine
options.D: Pain and stiffness in the joints

explanation: Skeletal fluorosis affects bones and joints, causing stiffness and pain, but it does not cause hair loss. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the main job of water in the human body?

options.A: Preventing all forms of mineral toxicity in the blood
options.B: Acting as the main fluid where body chemical reactions happen
options.C: Maintaining the structural rigidity of skeletal bones
options.D: Providing direct calories for cellular energy production

explanation: Water acts as the primary fluid environment where chemical reactions and metabolic processes take place in the body. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why are electrolytes important for how our bodies work?

options.A: They stop body temperature from rising during high fevers
options.B: They store extra fat calories for times of maternal starvation
options.C: They carry electrical charges that support nerve and muscle work
options.D: They create a thick protective barrier around internal organs

explanation: Minerals that act as electrolytes break down into charged ions, which are essential for nerve impulses and muscle contractions. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h1)

question: By about how much does total body water increase by the end of a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Zero liters, it actually decreases
options.B: Fifteen to twenty liters
options.C: One to two liters
options.D: Six to eight liters

explanation: Total body water expands significantly during pregnancy, increasing by about six to eight liters by term to support the growing baby. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the main reason pregnant women commonly get a mild form of anaemia?

options.A: Dietary intake of water completely replaces the need for iron
options.B: Plasma volume increases much faster than red blood cell mass
options.C: The bone marrow completely stops producing new red blood cells
options.D: The growing fetus destroys maternal red blood cells for iron

explanation: The rapid expansion of liquid plasma dilutes the concentration of red blood cells, causing a normal drop in hemoglobin levels. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which mineral is mainly responsible for regulating fluid volume outside of cells?

options.A: Magnesium
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Sodium
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Sodium is the major mineral outside the cells that dictates water distribution and overall fluid balance in the body. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h3)

question: A pregnant woman has severe leg cramps and a sensitive uterus. Which mineral shortage is often linked to this?

options.A: Bicarbonate
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Chloride
options.D: Magnesium

explanation: Magnesium plays a key role in muscle and nerve activity, and low levels often show up as painful cramps and a more irritable uterus. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h3)

question: Which organ is the main controller of water and mineral balance in the body?

options.A: Kidneys
options.B: Pancreas
options.C: Stomach
options.D: Liver

explanation: The kidneys continuously filter the blood, adjusting how much water and minerals are kept or removed to maintain stable body levels. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h4)

question: How does the hormone aldosterone help keep body fluids balanced?

options.A: By stopping the brain from registering thirst sensations
options.B: By increasing the heart rate to pump fluid faster
options.C: By telling the kidneys to hold onto sodium and water
options.D: By forcing the kidneys to flush out all available sodium

explanation: Aldosterone signals the kidney tubules to retain sodium, which naturally draws water back into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h4)

question: What does dark, concentrated urine usually mean in a pregnant woman?

options.A: An excess amount of sodium in the diet
options.B: Normal high levels of fetal iron storage
options.C: Rapid expansion of total body plasma
options.D: Not drinking enough fluids or being dehydrated

explanation: Concentrated, dark urine shows that the kidneys are working hard to save water because overall fluid intake is low. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why is checking a mother's pulse and blood pressure helpful when checking her hydration?

options.A: Fluid loss often causes a fast pulse and low blood pressure
options.B: Dehydration immediately stops the heart from beating normally
options.C: High blood pressure is the very first sign of mild water shortage
options.D: Pulse rates never change regardless of how much fluid is lost

explanation: When circulating fluid drops, the heart beats faster and blood pressure may fall due to the lower volume of blood. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h5)

question: What early pregnancy condition is a major cause of severe dehydration and mineral loss?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Physiological hemodilution
options.C: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Hyperemesis gravidarum involves severe, ongoing vomiting that quickly drains essential body fluids and minerals. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical sign of a severe fluid or mineral imbalance?

options.A: Confusion or mental changes in the mother
options.B: Muscle weakness and painful cramping in the limbs
options.C: Irregular heart rhythms found on examination
options.D: Normal, stable daily body weight with clear urine

explanation: Clear urine and a stable weight show good hydration, while muscle weakness, confusion, and irregular heartbeats point to imbalances. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h6)

question: Which foods are great natural sources of potassium for pregnant women?

options.A: Highly polished white rice
options.B: Bananas and oranges
options.C: Processed canned meats
options.D: Refined white sugar and oil

explanation: Fresh fruits like bananas and oranges are well-known natural sources of dietary potassium. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h7)

question: Why should midwives generally advise against strict salt restriction in a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnant women lose all their body fat if they avoid salt
options.B: Low salt diets always cause immediate gestational diabetes
options.C: Salt restriction causes the fetus to stop growing completely
options.D: Normal sodium is needed to support healthy fluid volume expansion

explanation: Pregnancy requires more body fluid, and cutting out salt can make it hard for the body to keep the extra fluid it needs. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h7)

question: What are the basic building blocks that make up protein molecules?

options.A: Amino acids
options.B: Nucleic acids
options.C: Fatty acids
options.D: Simple sugars

explanation: Proteins are constructed from long chains of amino acids linked together. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why must pregnant women eat protein every day instead of relying on stored reserves?

options.A: Hormones destroy stored protein during the first trimester
options.B: Stored protein is instantly converted into body fat
options.C: The body cannot store extra protein for later use
options.D: The placenta blocks the release of stored proteins

explanation: The body has no major storage depot for proteins, so regular dietary intake is needed to meet daily needs. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which type of amino acids must come from food because the body cannot make them?

options.A: Saturated amino acids
options.B: Simple amino acids
options.C: Non-essential amino acids
options.D: Essential amino acids

explanation: Essential amino acids cannot be made by the human body and must be supplied through diet. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h2)

question: What makes a food source a complete protein?

options.A: It contains only non-essential amino acids
options.B: It requires no digestion before absorption
options.C: It provides all the essential amino acids
options.D: It has zero fat content alongside high protein

explanation: Complete proteins supply every single essential amino acid that the human body cannot produce on its own. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which blood protein plays the main role in keeping fluid inside blood vessels and preventing tissue swelling?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Globulin
options.C: Fibrinogen
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Albumin is the chief plasma protein responsible for keeping fluid inside the blood vessels. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h3)

question: A pregnant woman has severe swelling in her legs not linked to pre-eclampsia. Which dietary shortage might cause this fluid shift?

options.A: Iron
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Protein

explanation: Low blood protein levels allow fluid to seep out of blood vessels and collect in body tissues. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a plant-based source of protein commonly found in local markets?

options.A: Beans and lentils
options.B: Root tubers like cassava
options.C: Fresh green vegetables
options.D: Ripe citrus fruits

explanation: Legumes like beans and lentils are rich plant sources of dietary protein. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do strict vegetarians need to eat a variety of different plant foods throughout the day?

options.A: To avoid building up toxic levels of non-essential proteins
options.B: To combine different plant foods that lack certain essential amino acids
options.C: To prevent the rapid digestion of single plant foods
options.D: To ensure they consume enough vitamin C for energy

explanation: Individual plant foods rarely contain every essential amino acid, so mixing different sources provides a complete profile. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is a direct fetal problem linked to long-term lack of protein in the mother's diet?

options.A: Early closure of cranial sutures
options.B: Congenital heart murmurs
options.C: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.D: Excessive birth weight

explanation: A lack of adequate building blocks stunts overall fetal growth and development inside the womb. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common sign of mild to moderate protein shortage in an expectant mother?

options.A: Swelling in the lower extremities
options.B: High sustained energy levels
options.C: Frequent episodes of illness
options.D: Generalized muscle weakness

explanation: Protein deficiency causes fatigue and weakness, not high sustained energy levels. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h5)

question: A pregnant woman in a community says she cannot afford meat or fish for protein. What is the most practical midwifery advice?

options.A: Combine local plant foods like beans and grains to get complete amino acids
options.B: Tell her to buy expensive imported protein powders instead
options.C: Inform her that humans do not actually need protein during pregnancy
options.D: Advise her to wait until after delivery to worry about protein intake

explanation: Combining affordable local plant sources provides a practical way to achieve balanced amino acid intake without buying expensive meat. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why is it important for midwives to address local dietary taboos during nutrition counseling?

options.A: To prove that traditional beliefs are always scientifically correct
options.B: To prevent women from avoiding nutritious protein foods due to cultural myths
options.C: To replace traditional cooking utensils with modern kitchen equipment
options.D: To encourage women to stop eating local crops entirely

explanation: Taboos often restrict pregnant women from eating valuable foods like eggs or meat, so correcting these myths improves maternal nutrition. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a primary characteristic of all dietary lipids?

options.A: They dissolve easily in water
options.B: They do not dissolve in water
options.C: They turn into sugar during digestion
options.D: They are primarily composed of water

explanation: Lipids are hydrophobic organic compounds, meaning they separate from water rather than dissolving in it. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body need a steady supply of dietary lipids?

options.A: To support the expansion of maternal tissues and hormones
options.B: To keep her body temperature constantly lower than normal
options.C: To prevent the kidneys from filtering out essential proteins
options.D: To completely replace the need for carbohydrates in her diet

explanation: During pregnancy, lipids are crucial for building new maternal tissues like the uterus and for producing necessary pregnancy hormones. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which type of fat is typically liquid at room temperature and contains double bonds?

options.A: Unsaturated fat
options.B: Saturated fat
options.C: Hydrogenated lard
options.D: Trans fat crystals

explanation: Unsaturated fats have carbon-carbon double bonds that prevent them from packing tightly, making them liquid at room temperature. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h2)

question: A pregnant woman asks which cooking oil is better for her heart health. What should the midwife recommend?

options.A: Unsaturated plant oil like groundnut or olive oil
options.B: Hydrogenated margarine stored at room temperature
options.C: Heavy animal fat drippings from beef
options.D: Palm oil packed with solid fats

explanation: Unsaturated plant oils help maintain healthy blood lipid profiles and are safer for cardiovascular health during pregnancy than heavy saturated fats. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why are certain fatty acids classified as essential in human nutrition?

options.A: The body cannot make them and must get them from food
options.B: They can only be produced inside the human liver
options.C: They are the only fats that do not provide any calories
options.D: They turn into solid fat immediately inside the stomach

explanation: Essential nutrients are those that the body cannot manufacture on its own, requiring regular dietary intake. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h3)

question: What happens to maternal stores of omega-3 fatty acids if a pregnant woman eats a diet very low in these nutrients?

options.A: The placenta will block all fat transfer to protect the mother
options.B: The pregnancy will instantly halt until she changes her diet
options.C: The fetus will draw omega-3s directly from maternal tissue stores
options.D: The mother's body will automatically manufacture new omega-3s from sugar

explanation: The developing fetus prioritizes nutrient acquisition, meaning it will deplete maternal reserves of essential fatty acids if dietary intake is lacking. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which specific fetal organ accumulates large amounts of omega-3 fatty acids, especially DHA, during the third trimester?

options.A: The stomach
options.B: The lungs
options.C: The kidneys
options.D: The brain

explanation: The developing brain and nervous system have a high concentration of lipids and demand large amounts of DHA late in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is the accumulation of subcutaneous fat late in pregnancy important for a newborn baby?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for breast milk in the first week
options.B: It prevents the baby from breathing too quickly outside the womb
options.C: It allows the baby to float more easily inside the amniotic fluid
options.D: It provides insulation and helps regulate body temperature after birth

explanation: Subcutaneous adipose tissue acts as insulation against the cooler external environment and provides an immediate energy source for the newborn. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which local food item is a particularly good and accessible source of omega-3 fatty acids for pregnant women in Nigeria?

options.A: Local oily fish like mackerel or sardine
options.B: Polished white garri from cassava
options.C: Highly refined white table sugar
options.D: Pure cornstarch mixed with water

explanation: Oily fish are rich sources of essential omega-3 fatty acids, which support fetal brain and eye development. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h5)

question: A pregnant woman asks her midwife for advice on how to improve her fat intake without buying expensive imported items. What is the best practical response?

options.A: Drink large cups of industrial machine oil every morning
options.B: Stop eating all forms of fat immediately to protect your heart
options.C: Add local ingredients like melon seeds (egusi) and groundnuts to meals
options.D: Rely entirely on synthetic vitamin pills bought from street vendors

explanation: Locally available oilseeds and nuts are rich, affordable sources of healthy fats and nutrients suited for maternal diets. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main difference between fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins in how the body handles them?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins are cleared rapidly through daily urination
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins pose a much higher risk of long-term toxicity
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins are stored in high amounts within the liver
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins dissolve in lipids and accumulate in body tissues

explanation: Because fat-soluble vitamins dissolve in fats, the body stores them in the liver and adipose tissue rather than quickly excreting them through urine. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is maternal vitamin D intake especially important for a developing fetus?

options.A: It directly synthesizes red blood cells in the fetal bone marrow
options.B: It prevents maternal oxidative stress within the placental bed
options.C: It regulates calcium homeostasis for fetal bone mineralization
options.D: It stimulates immediate cellular differentiation of skin layers

explanation: Vitamin D controls how calcium is absorbed and used, which is vital for building strong bones and teeth in the growing fetus. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which digestive substance is needed in the small intestine to help absorb fat-soluble vitamins?

options.A: Insulin hormone
options.B: Gastric acid
options.C: Salivary amylase
options.D: Bile salts

explanation: Bile salts break down large fat globules into smaller droplets, allowing fat-soluble vitamins to be properly absorbed by the gut. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h2)

question: A pregnant woman has a condition that makes it hard to digest fats. What will happen to her fat-soluble vitamin levels?

options.A: Levels will fluctuate rapidly based on her daily carbohydrate intake
options.B: Levels will spike dangerously high due to improper liver storage failure
options.C: Levels will remain normal because fat malabsorption only affects water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Levels will drop because these vitamins rely on dietary fat absorption pathways

explanation: Conditions that impair fat digestion or absorption will also block the uptake of vitamins A, D, E, and K, leading to deficiency. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which fat-soluble vitamin helps activate blood-clotting factors?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Vitamin E
options.C: Vitamin D
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: Vitamin K is essential for blood coagulation because it helps activate several clotting factors in the liver. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h3)

question: How does vitamin E protect maternal and fetal cells from damage?

options.A: By directly regulating the absorption of dietary calcium
options.B: By neutralizing free radicals as a lipid-soluble antioxidant
options.C: By stimulating the production of visual pigments in the retina
options.D: By acting as a hormone to control blood glucose levels

explanation: Vitamin E sits inside cell membranes and stops free radicals from destroying delicate fats within the cell structure. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is an early sign of vitamin A deficiency in pregnant women?

options.A: Muscle spasms
options.B: Bone softening
options.C: Bleeding gums
options.D: Night blindness

explanation: Difficulty seeing in dim light, known as night blindness, is typically the first sign that the body lacks sufficient vitamin A. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h4)

question: A newborn baby is bleeding from the umbilical stump and has bruising. Which vitamin deficiency is the midwife likely suspecting?

options.A: Vitamin E
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: Newborns have low vitamin K stores and sterile guts, putting them at risk of bleeding problems unless prophylactic vitamin K is administered. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which fat-soluble vitamin can cause birth defects if taken in high doses during the first trimester?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Vitamin E
options.C: Vitamin D
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: Preformed vitamin A in megadoses can cause birth defects when taken during early pregnancy, which is why prenatal supplements must be carefully regulated. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why does high intake of preformed vitamin A carry a risk of birth defects while eating beta-carotene from vegetables does not?

options.A: Plant carotene cannot cross the placental barrier under any circumstance
options.B: Preformed vitamin A destroys all circulating hormones in the placenta
options.C: Beta-carotene is water-soluble and gets immediately excreted through sweat
options.D: The body strictly regulates the conversion of plant carotene into active vitamin A

explanation: The body only converts as much beta-carotene into vitamin A as it needs, preventing the toxic buildup seen with preformed retinol supplements. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h5)

question: A pregnant woman at the antenatal clinic asks for an affordable local source of vitamin A. Which Nigerian food item is best to recommend?

options.A: Refined groundnut oil
options.B: Polished white rice
options.C: White cassava garri
options.D: Red palm oil

explanation: Unrefined red palm oil is an exceptionally rich, culturally accessible local source of provitamin A carotenoids. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main reason midwives in Nigeria should encourage diverse local foods instead of high-potency commercial supplements during pregnancy?

options.A: It minimizes the danger of vitamin toxicity while ensuring steady nutrient intake
options.B: Local foods are scientifically proven to cure all congenital malformations
options.C: Pregnant women cannot absorb synthetic vitamins under tropical weather
options.D: Commercial supplements are completely devoid of any fat-soluble vitamins

explanation: Promoting whole foods supplies essential nutrients safely without the risk of hypervitaminosis associated with unmonitored megadoses. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h6)

question: What happens to excess water-soluble vitamins in the human body?

options.A: They are filtered by the kidneys and passed out in the urine.
options.B: They turn directly into solid fat tissue beneath the skin.
options.C: They crystallize inside the joints and cause painful swelling.
options.D: They are stored safely inside the liver for future emergency use.

explanation: Because water-soluble vitamins do not stay long in the body, the kidneys clear out any extra amount through urine. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why must pregnant women consume water-soluble vitamins on a regular, daily basis?

options.A: The body does not store large amounts of them internally.
options.B: Unused vitamins immediately transform into toxic waste products.
options.C: High pregnancy hormones destroy stored vitamins overnight.
options.D: They prevent the stomach from absorbing any other food types.

explanation: Since these vitamins are quickly lost through bodily fluids, daily intake is required to maintain steady nutrient levels for mother and baby. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the alternative chemical name for Vitamin C?

options.A: Ascorbic acid
options.B: Thiamine
options.C: Folic acid
options.D: Cobalamin

explanation: Vitamin C is scientifically recognized as ascorbic acid, known for its strong antioxidant properties. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h2)

question: How do B-complex vitamins primarily assist cellular metabolism in the body?

options.A: They act as primary storage units for long-term body fat.
options.B: They generate body heat by blocking blood flow to the skin.
options.C: They form a hard physical shell around vulnerable cell walls.
options.D: They act as metabolic coenzymes to help drive chemical reactions.

explanation: B-vitamins function mainly as coenzymes that unlock energy from the foods we eat and support tissue growth. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which specific vitamin helps significantly with the absorption of plant-based iron?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Thiamine
options.C: Riboflavin
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Ascorbic acid enhances the bioavailability of non-heme iron found in plant foods, protecting against maternal anaemia. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h3)

question: A pregnant woman in her first trimester complains of severe morning sickness and fatigue. Which B-vitamin is especially valuable for supporting red blood cell formation and preventing early neural tube defects?

options.A: Biotin
options.B: Niacin
options.C: Thiamine
options.D: Folate

explanation: Folate is critical during early embryonic development to build red blood cells and close the neural tube properly. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h3)

question: What classic condition is caused by a severe dietary deficiency of Vitamin C?

options.A: Beri-beri
options.B: Pellagra
options.C: Scurvy
options.D: Rickets

explanation: Scurvy develops when low vitamin C impairs collagen production, leading to weak blood vessels and bleeding gums. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why does a lack of folate or Vitamin B12 result in megaloblastic anaemia?

options.A: It causes the bone marrow to stop producing blood cells completely overnight.
options.B: It makes the spleen destroy healthy red blood cells much too quickly.
options.C: It disrupts proper DNA synthesis, causing red blood cells to grow large and immature.
options.D: It blocks the stomach from taking in any water or liquid nutrients.

explanation: Both vitamins are essential for cell division; without them, red blood cells fail to divide properly and become oversized and ineffective. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following local Nigerian foods is an excellent source of dietary folate?

options.A: Fluted pumpkin leaves (ugu)
options.B: Processed table sugar
options.C: Refined white cassava garri
options.D: Bottled carbonated drinks

explanation: Dark green leafy vegetables like ugu are rich natural sources of folate needed during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is relying on a variety of local whole foods better than taking isolated supplements alone?

options.A: Whole foods provide a balanced mix of multiple vitamins, minerals, and fiber together.
options.B: Supplements are completely illegal to buy or sell in local Nigerian markets.
options.C: Whole foods contain heavy amounts of artificial preservatives for energy.
options.D: Synthetic vitamins cannot be absorbed by the human digestive tract at all.

explanation: Dietary variety ensures the pregnant woman receives synergistic nutrients that work together for optimal health. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h5)

question: How does prolonged boiling of green vegetables negatively affect their vitamin content?

options.A: It seals the vitamins tightly inside the plant fibers so they cannot be digested.
options.B: It destroys heat-sensitive B-vitamins and leaches them into the cooking water.
options.C: It turns the vitamins into heavy minerals that damage the stomach lining.
options.D: It converts all water-soluble vitamins into permanent fat reserves.

explanation: Boiling vegetables for too long breaks down vitamins like C and B-complex, especially if the cooking water is thrown away. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h6)

question: A pregnant woman asks her midwife the best fluid to swallow her routine iron and folate supplements with. What is the most appropriate advice to give her?

options.A: Swallow them with strong hot tea or coffee to calm the stomach.
options.B: Avoid taking any fluids with them to prevent dilution in the body.
options.C: Mix the crushed tablets directly into a cup of whole milk.
options.D: Take them with clean water or fresh citrus juice to help absorption.

explanation: Water or vitamin C-rich juice aids absorption, whereas substances like tea contain tannins that bind to nutrients and reduce their uptake. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the daily intake amount that defines a macro mineral?

options.A: Less than 50 milligrams daily
options.B: Exceeding 10 grams daily
options.C: Exactly 1 milligram daily
options.D: Exceeding 100 milligrams daily

explanation: Macro minerals are the minerals the body needs in larger amounts every day, specifically anything greater than 100 milligrams. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why do macro minerals need to work together in the body?

options.A: All macro minerals have the exact same chemical structure
options.B: Only one macro mineral can be absorbed by the intestines at a time
options.C: Minerals cancel each other out if consumed in the same meal
options.D: The proper function of one mineral often relies on the presence of others

explanation: Minerals like calcium and magnesium work closely together in the body, meaning a shortage of one can affect how well another works. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h1)

question: Where is most of the calcium in the human body stored?

options.A: Skeletal muscles
options.B: Bones and teeth
options.C: Liver and kidneys
options.D: Blood plasma

explanation: About 99 percent of the body's calcium is kept in the skeleton and teeth to give them strength. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h2)

question: How does a pregnant mother's body protect her baby if her diet lacks enough calcium?

options.A: It manufactures new calcium inside the placenta
options.B: It releases calcium from the mother's own bones into the bloodstream
options.C: It absorbs extra calcium from the mother's skin
options.D: It halts foetal bone growth until the mother eats more dairy

explanation: When dietary intake is too low, the body draws on calcium stored in the mother's bones to make sure the baby still gets enough. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which hormone increases during pregnancy to help the body absorb more calcium?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Calcitriol

explanation: Calcitriol is the active form of vitamin D. It increases during pregnancy to help the intestines absorb more calcium. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h3)

question: During which stage of pregnancy does the transfer of calcium to the baby happen the fastest?

options.A: At the moment of implantation
options.B: First trimester
options.C: Third trimester
options.D: During the postpartum period

explanation: The baby's bones grow the fastest during the last three months of pregnancy, which is when calcium needs are highest. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which local Nigerian food is a good source of calcium because it is eaten whole with its soft bones?

options.A: Pounded yam
options.B: White rice
options.C: Small dried fish
options.D: Cassava flakes

explanation: Eating small dried fish with their soft bones intact provides a very accessible source of dietary calcium. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why might dark green leafy vegetables provide less usable calcium than dairy products?

options.A: Plant oxalates can reduce how much calcium the body absorbs
options.B: Cooking vegetables destroys all mineral content instantly
options.C: The body cannot digest plant cell walls at all
options.D: Vegetables contain zero usable vitamins

explanation: Natural compounds called oxalates in some greens bind to calcium, making it harder for the intestines to take it up. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is a common early sign of low calcium levels during pregnancy?

options.A: Sudden weight loss
options.B: Excessive hair growth
options.C: Painful muscle cramps
options.D: Yellowing of the eyes

explanation: Low calcium affects the nerves and muscles, often showing up as painful spasms or cramps in the legs and feet. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which condition is NOT directly caused by long-term calcium loss in mothers?

options.A: Maternal bone mineral loss
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Osteopenia
options.D: Osteoporosis

explanation: Gestational diabetes is related to blood sugar and insulin, whereas calcium depletion directly affects bone density conditions like osteopenia and osteoporosis. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why should calcium supplements be taken at a different time from iron tablets?

options.A: Iron destroys the chemical structure of calcium
