options.B: 5% Dextrose water
options.C: Fruit juice dilution
options.D: ReSoMal

explanation: ReSoMal (Rehydration Solution for Malnutrition) contains less sodium and more potassium to match the altered electrolyte balance in malnourished children. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T2#BMP118_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is a key nutritional message midwives should promote to prevent kwashiorkor in Nigerian communities?

options.A: Relying exclusively on refined maize pap as the best food for toddlers
options.B: Stopping breastfeeding immediately at three months to introduce solid foods
options.C: Combining local starchy staples with affordable protein sources like beans and fish
options.D: Avoiding all local foods in favor of expensive imported infant formulas

explanation: Prevention centers on diversifying the diet by mixing accessible staple foods with quality local protein sources to prevent amino acid deficiencies. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T2#BMP118_U4_T2_h8)

question: How long is exclusive breastfeeding recommended before introducing complementary foods?

options.A: Up to one full year
options.B: The first six months of life
options.C: Until the child grows teeth
options.D: The first three months only

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding for six months provides optimal nutrition and immune protection before other foods are gradually introduced. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T2#BMP118_U4_T2_h8)

question: What is the primary dietary deficiency that causes marasmus?

options.A: Folic acid and Vitamin D
options.B: Water and essential salts
options.C: Total calories and protein
options.D: Vitamin C and iron only

explanation: Marasmus happens when a child lacks enough overall food and energy, leading to severe wasting of both fat and muscle tissue. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why does the body break down its own skeletal muscle during marasmus?

options.A: To store extra fat around organs
options.B: To supply amino acids for energy
options.C: To increase physical strength
options.D: To stimulate rapid bone growth

explanation: During starvation, muscle proteins are broken down so the body can turn them into glucose to keep vital organs working. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of marasmus in young infants?

options.A: Diluted and low-calorie cereal gruels
options.B: Early stopping of breast milk
options.C: Recurrent diarrhea infections
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding for six months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding protects against malnutrition. Stopping it early and giving poor foods triggers marasmus. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h2)

question: An infant has chronic diarrhea and rapid weight loss after being weaned early onto thin corn gruel. What best explains this?

options.A: The loop of low nutrient intake and gut infection
options.B: A genetic bone marrow disorder
options.C: An allergic reaction to milk protein
options.D: Normal weight changes in the first year

explanation: Diluted gruels lack proper energy, and diarrhea worsens nutrient loss, creating a continuous cycle of worsening starvation. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h2)

question: What facial appearance is classically seen in an infant with marasmus?

options.A: Old man face with sunken cheeks
options.B: Moon face with a rounded jaw
options.C: Swollen face with tight eyelids
options.D: Asymmetrical facial paralysis

explanation: The loss of facial fat pads creates a shrunken, wrinkled appearance often referred to as an old man's face. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h3)

question: How does the mental state of a child with marasmus usually differ from a child with kwashiorkor?

options.A: Marasmic infants show no emotion while others laugh
options.B: Marasmic infants are alert and irritable, whereas kwashiorkor children are apathetic
options.C: Both conditions cause the exact same extreme lethargy
options.D: Marasmic infants are in a coma while others are hyperactive

explanation: Children with marasmus stay mentally alert and often fret, whereas kwashiorkor causes marked apathy and lethargy. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which clinical sign is present in kwashiorkor but NOT in marasmus?

options.A: Irritable mental state
options.B: Swelling from fluid retention (edema)
options.C: Prominent rib cage
options.D: Severe muscle wasting

explanation: Fluid retention, or edema, is a hallmark of kwashiorkor but does not happen in marasmus. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why might a child with kwashiorkor appear heavier on a scale than a child with marasmus, even though both are severely malnourished?

options.A: Kwashiorkor children build excess bone density
options.B: Protein diets build rapid muscle
options.C: Fluid retention hides the true degree of tissue wasting
options.D: Fat storage remains untouched in the belly

explanation: Swelling from fluid accumulation adds extra weight on the scale, hiding how much muscle and fat the child has actually lost. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is a primary reason children with marasmus face a high risk of severe infections?

options.A: High levels of stomach acid
options.B: Suppressed immune function
options.C: Overactive white blood cell production
options.D: Excessive accumulation of body fat

explanation: Starvation shrinks immune organs, destroying the child's ability to fight off everyday infections. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why does refeeding a severely malnourished child require careful monitoring of potassium?

options.A: Potassium prevents leg swelling
options.B: Shifting metabolism can cause dangerous drops in blood potassium
options.C: Potassium stops the liver from storing fat
options.D: High potassium cures gut infections

explanation: When feeding restarts, cells rapidly take up potassium, which can crash blood levels and trigger heart problems if not monitored. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h5)

question: What specialized solution is preferred over standard oral rehydration salt solution when treating dehydration in severe marasmus?

options.A: Plain sterile water with high sodium
options.B: Undiluted cow's milk with sugar
options.C: ReSoMal (Rehydration for Malnutrition)
options.D: Fruit juice with iron

explanation: ReSoMal has lower sodium and higher potassium than standard oral rehydration salt, which protects a weak heart from fluid overload. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h6)

question: A newly admitted infant with marasmus is ravenous and demands large feeds immediately. What is the safest action for the midwife?

options.A: Provide small, frequent feeds using F-75 formula
options.B: Restrict all food and water for forty-eight hours
options.C: Feed the child large family meals for fast weight gain
options.D: Give rapid intravenous fluids

explanation: A starved gut cannot handle large meals at once. Starting with small, frequent low-solute feeds prevents dangerous refeeding complications. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h6)

question: At what age should exclusive breastfeeding ideally be supplemented with other foods?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Twelve months
options.C: Nine months
options.D: Three months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first six months of life, after which safe and nutritious complementary foods should be introduced. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h7)

question: How do regular growth monitoring sessions help prevent marasmus in a community?

options.A: By providing instant surgery for birth defects
options.B: By offering high-dose antibiotics to every child
options.C: By identifying weight loss early before severe wasting develops
options.D: By eliminating local poverty

explanation: Plotting growth curves helps health workers spot slowing weight gain early, allowing counseling and intervention before severe malnutrition sets in. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which part of the blood increases the most during pregnancy, leading to hemodilution?

options.A: Platelets
options.B: Plasma
options.C: White blood cells
options.D: Red blood cells

explanation: Plasma volume increases much faster than red blood cell mass during pregnancy, diluting the blood concentration and leading to physiological anemia. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why do pregnant women experience a natural drop in their hemoglobin levels?

options.A: To make room for the growing fetus in the womb
options.B: As a result of decreased fluid intake during early gestation
options.C: Due to the rapid destruction of iron stores by the placenta
options.D: Because plasma increases much more than red blood cells

explanation: The fluid portion of blood expands significantly more than the cellular portion, creating a dilution effect that lowers measured hemoglobin levels. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the single most common cause of anemia in pregnant women in Nigeria?

options.A: Vitamin C deficiency
options.B: Calcium shortage
options.C: Folate overload
options.D: Iron deficiency

explanation: Inadequate dietary iron intake combined with the high demands of pregnancy makes iron deficiency the primary driver of anemia locally. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h2)

question: How do parasitic infections like malaria and hookworm contribute to anemia in pregnancy?

options.A: By stopping the placenta from producing progesterone
options.B: By destroying red blood cells and causing chronic blood loss
options.C: By increasing the speed of plasma production in the liver
options.D: By blocking the absorption of water in the large intestine

explanation: Malaria parasites destroy red blood cells, while hookworms cause chronic intestinal blood loss, both depleting the body's iron reserves. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h2)

question: Where is pallor most reliably checked during a physical examination of a pregnant woman?

options.A: The back of the hands and knees
options.B: The forehead and upper chest
options.C: The conjunctivae and palm creases
options.D: The tip of the nose and earlobes

explanation: Mucous membranes like the conjunctiva and areas with thin skin like palm creases show reduced color best when a patient is anemic. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks gestation complains of severe fatigue, dizziness, and palpitations when walking short distances. What underlying condition do these symptoms most strongly suggest?

options.A: Normal physiological changes
options.B: Severe anemia
options.C: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Palpitations, dizziness, and fatigue during mild activity are classic signs of poor tissue oxygenation caused by low hemoglobin. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h3)

question: What does a Packed Cell Volume (PCV) test measure in a blood sample?

options.A: The amount of sugar dissolved in the blood plasma
options.B: The speed at which white blood cells fight off infections
options.C: The percentage of blood volume made up of red blood cells
options.D: The exact total volume of blood circulating in the heart

explanation: PCV measures the proportion of red blood cells relative to the total volume of whole blood. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is it important to repeat hemoglobin screening at later stages of pregnancy?

options.A: To catch new or worsening anemia as fetal demands increase
options.B: To measure the exact weight gain of the developing baby
options.C: To check if the placenta has attached properly to the uterus
options.D: To confirm the exact gestational age of the fetus

explanation: Nutritional needs rise sharply as pregnancy progresses, meaning a woman with normal blood levels early on can easily develop anemia later. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h4)

question: How does severe maternal anemia directly increase the risk of postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: The tired uterine muscle fails to contract effectively after delivery
options.B: Blood pressure rises so high that blood vessels burst in the pelvis
options.C: The baby's blood mixes with the mother's blood during the third stage
options.D: The placenta becomes too thick to detach from the uterine wall

explanation: An anemic myometrium lacks sufficient oxygen and energy to clamp down firmly on blood vessels after the placenta separates, leading to excessive bleeding. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common fetal complication linked to untreated maternal anemia?

options.A: Low birth weight
options.B: Macrosomia
options.C: Premature birth
options.D: Intrauterine growth restriction

explanation: Anemia starves the fetus of oxygen and nutrients, leading to small babies (low birth weight and growth restriction), not excessively large ones (macrosomia). [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is a common harmless side effect of oral iron supplements that midwives should explain to patients?

options.A: Temporary loss of taste
options.B: Numbness in the fingers
options.C: Bright yellow urine coloration
options.D: Dark or black-colored stools

explanation: Unabsorbed iron passes through the digestive tract and turns the stool a dark green or black color, which is completely harmless. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h6)

question: A woman at 36 weeks gestation presents with a packed cell volume of 21 percent and signs of severe weakness. What intervention is most appropriate given her advanced gestational age and low reading?

options.A: Immediate induction of labor without any blood investigation
options.B: Advice to eat more green vegetables and return in one month
options.C: Urgent medical review for parenteral iron or blood transfusion
options.D: Discontinuation of all iron supplements to rest the stomach

explanation: Severe anemia late in pregnancy requires rapid correction before labor begins, making oral supplements alone too slow to protect her. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why should a pregnant woman avoid drinking tea or coffee immediately after taking her iron supplement?

options.A: Substances in tea and coffee reduce the body's ability to absorb iron
options.B: Hot liquids wash away the protective lining of the stomach wall
options.C: Caffeine causes the iron tablets to dissolve too quickly in the mouth
options.D: The combination triggers severe allergic reactions in the skin

explanation: Tannins found in tea and coffee bind to iron in the digestive tract, preventing it from being properly absorbed into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which food component helps improve the body's absorption of dietary iron when eaten together?

options.A: Caffeine
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Fiber

explanation: Vitamin C creates an acidic environment in the gut that converts iron into a form that is much easier for the body to absorb. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h7)

question: What primary body chemical does the thyroid gland use iodine to manufacture?

options.A: Estrogen and progesterone
options.B: Cortisol and aldosterone
options.C: Thyroid hormones
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: Iodine is an essential building block that the thyroid gland directly uses to create thyroxine and triiodothyronine. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why does a lack of dietary iodine cause the thyroid gland to grow larger?

options.A: Excess water accumulation causes the gland to expand rapidly
options.B: The gland enlarges to capture more circulating iodine from the blood
options.C: Infection inflames the tissue and increases overall gland size
options.D: Cell death forces the gland to produce scar tissue and swell

explanation: When iodine is scarce, the brain signals the thyroid to grow larger in an attempt to trap any remaining iodine from the blood. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h1)

question: During which stage of pregnancy does the developing baby rely completely on the mother's thyroid hormones?

options.A: Second trimester
options.B: First trimester
options.C: Third trimester
options.D: Immediate postpartum

explanation: The baby's thyroid gland does not function yet during early pregnancy, making early brain development depend entirely on the mother's supply. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h2)

question: What happens to the body's handling of iodine during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Kidneys retain all iodine to prevent any loss through urine
options.B: Kidneys convert excess iodine into stored liver reserves
options.C: Kidneys stop processing iodine entirely until after delivery
options.D: Kidneys excrete more iodine due to a higher filtration rate

explanation: Increased blood flow to the kidneys during pregnancy causes more iodine to be filtered out in urine, which increases the daily nutritional requirement. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the most severe physical and neurological effect of a severe iodine shortage during fetal life?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Endemic cretinism
options.C: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: A severe lack of iodine during early development permanently damages the nervous system, leading to a condition called endemic cretinism. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following problems is NOT a typical sign of iodine deficiency in adults?

options.A: Permanent physical dwarfism
options.B: Enlarged thyroid gland or goiter
options.C: Reduced mental alertness
options.D: Sluggishness and low energy

explanation: Physical dwarfism is linked to deficiencies that affect skeletal growth during childhood development, while adults experience other symptoms like fatigue and goiter. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h3)

question: What physical sign indicates a Grade 2 goiter during a routine neck check in antenatal care?

options.A: The thyroid is completely invisible and cannot be felt by hand
options.B: The swelling can only be felt when the woman swallows water
options.C: The swelling is clearly visible with the neck in a normal position
options.D: The swelling only appears when the woman extends her neck backward

explanation: A Grade 2 goiter is large enough to be seen easily without needing to feel the neck or tilt the head back. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h4)

question: A pregnant woman at her first clinic visit has a visibly enlarged thyroid gland without touching it. How should the midwife grade this finding?

options.A: Grade 2
options.B: Grade 3
options.C: Grade 1
options.D: Grade 0

explanation: When a goiter is visible during normal posture, it is classified as Grade 2 under standard assessment guidelines. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h4)

question: How does untreated iodine deficiency in pregnancy affect a newborn's future learning potential?

options.A: It accelerates brain growth so much that the child develops severe headaches
options.B: It permanently prevents the child from learning to speak any language
options.C: It can lower intelligence quotient and cause learning difficulties in school
options.D: It causes severe blindness and hearing loss within the first year of life

explanation: Not having enough thyroid hormone during key brain development windows limits neural pathways, which can affect learning later in childhood. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which serious pregnancy complication is frequently linked to a lack of maternal iodine?

options.A: Placental attachment abnormalities
options.B: Excessive amniotic fluid accumulation
options.C: Spontaneous abortion and stillbirth
options.D: Premature rupture of the membranes

explanation: Severe shortages of thyroid hormones disrupt normal pregnancy progression, leading to higher rates of fetal loss. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the main public health strategy used to eliminate iodine deficiency in communities?

options.A: Mandatory weekly fasting periods
options.B: Universal Salt Iodization
options.C: Routine boiling of all drinking water
options.D: Daily intravenous iodine injections

explanation: Adding iodine to household salt ensures that entire communities get a steady daily intake with minimal cost or behavior change. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is public health education on storing iodized salt important in tropical climates?

options.A: Humidity causes the salt to melt into a liquid form immediately
options.B: Heat and moisture can cause iodine to evaporate or degrade from the salt
options.C: Sunlight turns the salt toxic if containers are left transparent
options.D: Insects consume the iodine crystals if the salt bag remains open

explanation: Environmental heat and humidity break down iodine compounds in poorly stored salt, reducing its nutritional value. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h6)

question: A pregnant woman mentions she buys cheap, unsealed market salt because it costs less. What is the best action for the midwife?

options.A: Advise her to switch to certified iodized salt and explain how heat and moisture destroy poor-quality salt
options.B: Prescribe an immediate blood test to check her current thyroid hormone levels
options.C: Recommend that she stop eating salt completely to avoid swelling in her legs and feet
options.D: Tell her that all salt has the exact same amount of iodine regardless of where she buys it

explanation: Midwives help mothers by explaining the importance of using certified iodized salt and storing it properly to protect against deficiency. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h7)

question: What cooking advice should a midwife share regarding the use of iodized salt?

options.A: Add the salt toward the end of cooking to protect the iodine from excessive heat
options.B: Dissolve the salt in cold water and discard the water before eating
options.C: Fry the salt in oil first before adding vegetables to seal the minerals in
options.D: Keep the cooking pot tightly sealed with heavy stones while boiling

explanation: Long exposure to high heat during cooking can cause iodine to escape as gas, reducing the health benefits of the salt. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which plant-based form of Vitamin A is commonly found in fruits and vegetables?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Retinol
options.C: Beta-carotene
options.D: Ergocalciferol

explanation: Beta-carotene acts as a provitamin A carotenoid in plant foods, which the body then converts into active vitamin A. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why do the nutritional needs for vitamin A increase during pregnancy?

options.A: To support fetal tissue growth and maternal health
options.B: To prevent gestational diabetes mellitus from developing
options.C: To increase total circulating blood volume immediately
options.D: To directly stimulate the production of breast milk before birth

explanation: The developing fetus requires adequate vitamin A for tissue development, alongside supporting the mother's own physiological changes. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which Nigerian food staple is naturally very rich in beta-carotene and commonly used in daily cooking?

options.A: Red palm oil
options.B: Polished white rice
options.C: White cassava garri
options.D: Refined vegetable oil

explanation: Unprocessed red palm oil contains high levels of beta-carotene, making it a powerful local dietary source of vitamin A. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why might a pregnant woman who eats plenty of green vegetables still show signs of low vitamin A?

options.A: Her stomach acid is too strong for plant cell walls to open
options.B: Cooking vegetables completely destroys all available carotenoids
options.C: Her diet lacks sufficient dietary fat to help absorb the nutrients
options.D: Green leafy vegetables only contain water-soluble vitamins

explanation: Because vitamin A is fat-soluble, the digestive tract needs dietary fats present to properly absorb carotenoids from plant sources. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the earliest clinical sign of vitamin A deficiency in pregnant women?

options.A: Total blindness
options.B: Corneal scarring
options.C: Bitot's spots
options.D: Night blindness

explanation: Difficulty seeing in dim light or at dusk is typically the first warning sign that vitamin A stores are critically low. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h3)

question: What do Bitot's spots look like on the eye?

options.A: Foamy, triangular patches on the conjunctiva
options.B: Deep ulcers forming directly on the iris
options.C: Tiny red bleeding spots under the eyelid
options.D: Cloudy white rings surrounding the cornea

explanation: Bitot's spots are dry, foamy keratin accumulations on the surface of the eye membrane associated with moderate to severe deficiency. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h3)

question: How does vitamin A deficiency weaken the body's defense against infections?

options.A: It prevents the kidneys from filtering bacterial toxins
options.B: It damages mucosal barriers and reduces protective secretions
options.C: It directly stops the bone marrow from making platelets
options.D: It destroys circulating red blood cells in the bloodstream

explanation: Vitamin A is essential for maintaining healthy epithelial tissues and mucus production, which trap and expel germs in the respiratory and gut tracts. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which childhood infection is often made much worse by a lack of vitamin A?

options.A: Tetanus
options.B: Measles
options.C: Chickenpox
options.D: Pertussis

explanation: Measles depletes vitamin A levels rapidly, and deficiency during the infection frequently leads to severe eye damage and high illness rates. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the most practical way for midwives in primary care clinics to check for early vitamin A deficiency?

options.A: Asking about vision changes in dim light
options.B: Ordering complex liver biopsy procedures
options.C: Measuring dark-adaptation speeds with lasers
options.D: Checking daily urine specific gravity

explanation: Screening for night blindness through simple questioning is an effective method for identifying deficiency during community clinic visits. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why must midwives be careful when recommending vitamin A supplements to pregnant women?

options.A: Excessive preformed retinol can cause birth defects
options.B: Pregnant women cannot absorb any oral vitamin capsules
options.C: High doses completely stop breast milk production
options.D: Supplements neutralize the effects of routine iron pills

explanation: High therapeutic doses of preformed vitamin A can harm the developing fetus, unlike dietary beta-carotene from vegetables. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T6#BMP118_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard public health strategy used to control vitamin A deficiency?

options.A: Industrial fortification of staple food items
options.B: High-dose capsule supplementation programs
options.C: Mandatory surgical removal of the tear ducts
options.D: Promoting dietary diversification at home

question: What two measurements are required to calculate a pregnant woman's Body Mass Index?

options.A: Height and arm circumference
options.B: Weight and waist size
options.C: Weight and height
options.D: Blood pressure and weight

explanation: BMI is determined using a person's body mass in kilograms divided by the square of their height in meters. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why is measuring waist circumference useful for checking health risks?

options.A: It shows total body fat percentage.
options.B: It shows the amount of fat around internal organs.
options.C: It calculates daily food calories.
options.D: It measures upper body muscle mass.

explanation: Abdominal fat surrounding the internal organs carries a much higher metabolic risk than subcutaneous fat under the skin. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which body chemical pathway is affected by signals from stressed fat cells?

options.A: Oxytocin release
options.B: Thyroid regulation
options.C: Insulin signaling
options.D: Prolactin secretion

explanation: Inflammatory chemicals released by excess fat tissue interfere with how cells respond to insulin, causing resistance. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h2)

question: What does the pancreas do when a person develops severe insulin resistance?

options.A: It stops making digestive enzymes.
options.B: It produces extra insulin to overcome the resistance.
options.C: It turns stored fat into muscle.
options.D: It shrinks from lack of use.

explanation: To compensate for cells ignoring insulin, the pancreas works harder and secretes higher volumes of insulin into the blood. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which of these conditions is NOT typically linked to long-term obesity?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes
options.B: Abnormal blood fats
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: High blood pressure

explanation: Anemia is related to iron or nutrient deficiencies, whereas diabetes, high blood pressure, and abnormal blood fats are classic weight-linked conditions. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h3)

question: A clinic client has high blood pressure, high blood sugar, and extra belly weight. What underlying process connects these?

options.A: Metabolic disruption from excess fat
options.B: Too much physical exercise
options.C: Severe dehydration
options.D: A bacterial infection

explanation: These signs together reflect metabolic syndrome, driven largely by the systemic effects of excess adipose tissue. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h3)

question: What term describes the birth of an abnormally large baby, often linked to maternal diabetes?

options.A: Microcephaly
options.B: Hydrocephalus
options.C: Macrosomia
options.D: Apgar syndrome

explanation: Macrosomia refers to a newborn with an excessive birth weight, commonly defined as over 4,000 grams. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why does maternal obesity increase the risk of shoulder dystocia during delivery?

options.A: Excess fetal growth makes the baby too large to pass smoothly.
options.B: Amniotic fluid dries up before labor.
options.C: Pelvic bones fuse together from hormones.
options.D: The mother lacks strength to push.

explanation: High blood sugar crosses the placenta and makes the baby store extra fat, making the shoulders too wide to fit easily through the pelvis. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is a safe physical activity to recommend to a healthy pregnant woman for weight management?

options.A: Heavy weightlifting
options.B: Scuba diving
options.C: Brisk walking
options.D: Competitive sprinting

explanation: Moderate aerobic exercises like walking are safe, low-impact ways to maintain fitness and improve insulin sensitivity during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why are healthy lifestyle changes preferred over crash diets for pregnant women?

options.A: Restrictive dieting can deprive the developing baby of vital nutrients.
options.B: Pregnant women cannot follow diet plans.
options.C: Crash diets cause permanent weight loss immediately.
options.D: Food restrictions stop all placental hormone changes.

explanation: Pregnancy has high nutritional demands, so extreme food restriction risks harming fetal growth and maternal health. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the main reason why proper nutrition is so important during the postpartum period?

options.A: Lowering baseline maternal blood pressure
options.B: Supporting tissue healing and milk production
options.C: Preventing future childhood infections
options.D: Accelerating infant dental eruption

explanation: After delivery, the body needs extra nutrients to repair reproductive tissues and produce enough breast milk for the baby. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why should midwives take cultural food taboos into account when advising a mother on her diet?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing imported food items
options.B: To prove that modern medical science is superior to traditional beliefs
options.C: To completely eliminate local foods from the hospital kitchen routine
options.D: To respect traditions while ensuring the mother still gets the nutrients she needs

explanation: Acknowledging local beliefs helps build trust with the mother so she is more likely to accept and eat the recommended foods. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which diet is best for a mother right after major abdominal surgery when her bowel sounds are still very low?

options.A: Full liquid diet
options.B: Clear liquid diet
options.C: High protein diet
options.D: Soft mechanical diet

explanation: Clear liquids are very easy to digest and place minimal workload on a recovering digestive system. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h2)

question: What dietary change is typically expected for a pregnant patient diagnosed with gestational diabetes?

options.A: Controlled carbohydrate intake with balanced fiber
options.B: High sugar content to prevent sudden fainting spells
options.C: Unlimited portions of refined cassava and white rice
options.D: Strict exclusion of all dietary liquids and broths

explanation: Managing blood sugar involves eating steady amounts of carbohydrates combined with fiber to prevent rapid glucose spikes. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why is Vitamin C often given alongside iron supplements when treating anemia in pregnancy?

options.A: It prevents the common side effect of maternal constipation
options.B: It masks the metallic taste of iron supplements in the mouth
options.C: It directly increases the total volume of amniotic fluid
options.D: It significantly improves the absorption of iron in the gut

explanation: Vitamin C creates an acidic environment in the stomach that helps the body absorb iron much more efficiently. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is a high-protein diet especially important for a mother recovering from a Caesarean section?

options.A: To completely eliminate postpartum abdominal swelling within days
options.B: To promote rapid cellular repair and surgical wound healing
options.C: To prevent the development of postpartum gestational diabetes
options.D: To thicken breast milk so the baby sleeps for longer hours

explanation: Proteins supply the essential building blocks needed to repair damaged skin and muscle tissues after surgery. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is a major benefit of using centralized hospital kitchens in maternity wards?

options.A: Guaranteed preference for local traditional recipes by patients
options.B: Complete elimination of the need for nursing supervision
options.C: Precise control over therapeutic diet portions and nutrients
options.D: Elimination of all delays in food delivery during emergencies

explanation: Central kitchens can measure exact ingredients, making it much easier to follow doctor orders for specialized diets. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h4)

question: What common issue arises when family members bring most of a hospitalized patient's meals?

options.A: The cost of hospital admission automatically increases for the patient
options.B: The nutritional value of the food becomes completely standardized
options.C: It becomes difficult to monitor adherence to prescribed medical restrictions
options.D: The hospital kitchen staff lose their jobs due to reduced workload

explanation: Relatives might unknowingly bring restricted items, such as extra salt or sugar, that interfere with the medical treatment plan. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which quick measurement is commonly used in maternity clinics to screen for maternal undernutrition?

options.A: Total body bone density scan
options.B: Serum electrolyte blood panel test
options.C: Fasting blood glucose concentration
options.D: Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC)

explanation: MUAC is a fast, reliable, and non-invasive tool for checking nutritional status in pregnant and postpartum women. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h5)

question: A midwife notices a new mother has left her meat and fish untouched for three days. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Explore the underlying reason for refusing protein and offer acceptable alternatives
options.B: Discharge the patient immediately for refusing hospital food provisions
options.C: Report the mother to the hospital security personnel for wastefulness
options.D: Document that the patient is fully compliant with all ward routines

explanation: Finding out why the food is refused helps the midwife offer nutritious alternatives that the mother will actually eat. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why might offering smaller, frequent meals work better for a tired postpartum mother than three large plates?

options.A: It reduces the total daily financial budget of the hospital kitchen
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will sleep through the entire night
options.C: It prevents overwhelming a weak appetite and reduces feelings of nausea
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any nursing staff supervision

explanation: Large portions can seem daunting to an exhausted or nauseated patient, while small portions are much easier to manage. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical reason why hospitalized mothers reject standard hospital meals?

options.A: Guaranteed excess daily caloric intake
options.B: Unfamiliar taste or preparation style
options.C: Physical exhaustion after prolonged labor
options.D: Cultural or religious food restrictions

explanation: Hospital meals are rarely rejected because of too many calories; rather, issues like poor taste, temperature, and fatigue are the main barriers. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the main responsibility of a clinical dietitian in a hospital maternity setting?

options.A: Designing specialized therapeutic meal plans and calculating precise nutrients
options.B: Discharging patients and settling their hospital financial bills
options.C: Conducting routine vaginal examinations and monitoring active labor
options.D: Administering intravenous medications during emergency surgical procedures

explanation: Dietitians specialize in nutrition science and create precise dietary prescriptions for various medical conditions. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h7)

question: Why is regular communication between the midwife and the dietitian so important for patient recovery?

options.A: The midwife provides daily bedside feeding observations that help the dietitian adjust the meal plan
options.B: Collaborating prevents the hospital from purchasing any fresh food items locally
options.C: Midwives need dietitians to approve every routine nursing procedure performed at night
options.D: The dietitian is the only staff member permitted to document vital signs on the ward

explanation: Because midwives see what the patient actually eats every day, their feedback is vital for the dietitian to fine-tune the meals. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h7)
